_comment: The self-deploy manifest (DR-0236): repo-declared NAS services the services-sync loop installs/repairs on the NAS's own clock. Each entry is an IDEMPOTENT installer script (safe to run every cycle; every step no-ops when already done). Adding a service here + merging to main IS its deploy -- the nas mirror pulls, services-sync runs the installer, the service starts. 'enabled' is the committed greenlight. Installers never edit configs they cannot verify (DR-0076).

services.name: transcript-trickle
services.description: Drain the transcript backlog (2026-08-05 harvest review: 81/858 transcribed, loader parked on a manual app button while the CI path is YouTube-IP-blocked). Rides the ALREADY-ARMED services-sync clock (choir-dates pattern, zero new DSM entries): stamp-gated to ~8 fires/day x 4 captions from the NAS's residential IP (~32 videos/day = ~64-96 HTTP calls against the measured ~180/day IpBlocked ceiling), draining ~770 gaps in ~4 weeks then keeping pace with the channel. Registered FIRST so a slow sibling (docker pull, the choir-dates drain) can never starve it before the cycle-wide timeout. Loader carries --max budget + single-flight lock + a TIME-DECAYED backoff that clears itself (DR-0248; the 2026-08-06 fix -- the previous human-cleared pause pointed at ops-runner.py, which nothing installs, so it would have stopped the drain permanently and silently). Witness: harvest-health.yml probes the count from OUTSIDE the NAS and files an incident when it stops advancing.

services.name: ops-runner
services.description: Drain the app's operations queue (DR-0088 ops_commands) on the ALREADY-ARMED services-sync clock. Measured 2026-08-31: the queue's last row was 2026-07-06 and a zero-effect probe (unknown job, which the runner marks 'skipped' without executing) sat 'queued' with started_at NULL past a 60s poll -- the runner was dead for eight weeks. The cause was already written down in this file's own transcript-trickle note: 'ops-runner.py, which is installed by nothing.' DR-0088 shipped it inactive and armed by hand as a DSM boot task, and a hand-placed daemon does not survive a reboot; every other service here self-deploys, this one was never registered. The fix is NO daemon: --once per cycle, so there is nothing to outlive a reboot and nothing to re-arm (DR-0236/DR-0247). Latency moves from ~1 min to <=15 min, which is invisible for the two whitelisted jobs and is the whole distance between 'usually nothing' and 'every time.' Brakes unchanged (3/cycle budget, subprocess timeout, single-instance lock) plus the cycle timeout above; the runner's human-cleared pause becomes TIME-DECAYED so it can no longer stop the lane permanently and silently (DR-0248, the transcript-trickle precedent). Witness: ops-queue-health.yml probes the queue from OUTSIDE the NAS and files an incident when a command sits queued.

services.name: agent-consumer
services.description: The box agent (DR-0132 P1, built 2026-08-15 on Darrell's arm: 'you arm it dont make it not work to start'). Drains agent_tasks (migration 0137) through the DIRECT Postgres pooler -- measured open while the REST gateway is 402-restricted, so the Ask-the-models pane answers BEFORE the Aug 23 reset -- and serves @local on the NAS's own Ollama (Up 5 weeks, 127.0.0.1:11434) with keep_alive 0 (DR-0012). Deterministic class per DR-0248: --max budget + single-flight lock, no kill-switch. Keyless vendor rows FAIL with the why instead of spinning (the pane's honesty rules, mirrored server-side; selftest 12/12 gates merge in ci.yml). Credential placed by nas-agent-arm.yml over remote-hands; absent env = polite no-op naming exactly what is missing.

services.name: supabase
services.description: The SOVEREIGN Supabase stack (DR-0306). Born 2026-08-14: the hosted free tier restricted the project for exceeding its egress quota and locked all 23 users out of all four apps for 86 hours; Darrell: 'I'm not paying them... other options!!!!!!!?' -> 'start the NAS supabase stack.' Self-hosted Supabase serves the IDENTICAL API, so cutover is a URL + anon key rather than a rewrite -- measured: 196 .from(), 68 .auth, 64 .rpc(), 3 .storage, 2 .channel, all unchanged, and RLS stays enforced by Postgres so DR-0060's guard carries over. Eight containers on their own supabase-net, every port bound 127.0.0.1 ONLY (8800 kong / 5433 postgres / 8801 studio -- all clear of the ports measured live on this NAS), data under /volume1/docker/supabase. NOTHING POINTS AT IT YET, deliberately: standing it up proves it works and costs nothing, while the cutover stays a separate deliberate step so a half-proven stack can never take the family's app down. Secrets minted ONCE by the stdlib-only mint_keys.py (root cannot import dpoe's site-packages on this box) and never re-minted over a live stack -- re-minting JWT_SECRET signs out every user at once. The installer PROVES rather than claims: it polls the gateway's /auth/v1/health and exits non-zero with `compose ps` if it never answers 200. Selftest (12 checks, 2 proven-to-catch) gates merge in ci.yml. Runbook: infra/nas-supabase/README.md.

services.name: mcp
services.description: Sovereign MCP server (poetech-mcp.service on 127.0.0.1:8795, MCP 2026-07-28 stateless, READ-ONLY v1 over dispatch reel / task snapshot / Cage brake view) + token + venv + best-effort Caddy /mcp snippet. DR-0244.

services.name: scribe
services.description: Scribe ingest server (poetech-scribe.service on 127.0.0.1:8791) + data dir + token + venv + best-effort Caddy /scribe/* snippet. Pairs with the scribe-transcribe loop (the braked whisper-queue consumer).

services.name: property-photos
services.description: Sovereign property/family/album photo image server (photo_server.py, poetech-photo-server.service on 127.0.0.1:8099, reached via the same-origin /nas-photos route). Ends the 'NAS deploy pending Darrell' hand-deploy class: merge installs/repairs/starts it (DR-0268). Token kept, never regenerated over a live one.

services.name: tax-upload
services.description: The sovereign /taxes/* backend for Books -> Taxes (upload POST + archive.json + printable PDF reads), closing the 2026-09-06 "I am also unable to upload my taxes" defect. Root cause was NOT the app: tax_upload_server.py had no installer and appeared in no manifest, the Funnel carried no /taxes path mount (RECORDED-STATE listed only /, /mcp, /nas-photos), and the Caddy route existed only in a docstring -- so the upload POST hit a backend that was never started and the archive GET fell through the Funnel root to n8n, which is why one screen said 'could not reach the NAS upload service' and 'NO RETURNS INDEXED YET' at once. Same class as the /nas-photos gap (DR-0268): built, correct, never actuated. Not the three-brakes class -- request-driven only, no timer, no compute spawned, no work done until a browser asks. Installer is idempotent, reuses the EXISTING family bridge token (never regenerates over a live one), publishes any already-dropped returns on the cycle, mounts /taxes on the funnel additively, and probes 127.0.0.1:8790/health. Witness: site-health's outside-in probe plus the health route the installer curls.

services.name: funnel
services.description: Ensure the public Funnel serves the RECORDED-STATE sovereign rows (/mcp, /nas-photos) — the funnel_watchdog.py restore riding the ALREADY-ARMED services-sync clock, so the 2026-08-03 dark-funnel class heals with ZERO new DSM entries (Darrell: humans don't do anything). Idempotent and silent when the endpoint answers; bounded re-assert + one package restart when dark (DR-0268; RECORDED-STATE rule 1).

services.name: choir-dates
services.description: Drain the undated choir_sermons backlog (2026-08-04): yt-dlp reads each video's own release/upload stamp from the NAS's residential IP (CI runners are bot-checked and the stored Data-API key is rejected), PATCHes service_date ONLY where NULL via the youtube_load.py REST helpers, ~90 videos per 15-min cycle until drained, then a DONE marker no-ops every later cycle. Budget in-script (chunk + time), lock/timeout in the runner (DR-0248). Selftest gates merge in ci.yml.

services.name: ytzero
services.description: YT Zero (ghcr.io/pelski/ytzero pinned 0.25.3) -- sovereign chosen-channels-only YouTube inbox on host port 3701. Public RSS -> own SQLite at /volume1/docker/ytzero; no Google account, no API key, no recommendation feed; optional yt-dlp downloads; LAN/Tailscale only. Runbook: infra/nas-ytzero/README.md.
